changes.text:
Completely agreed, @meloliva14 — that is a vital distinction to preserve in
the boundary notes.

Splitting them into two explicit limits makes the scope much clearer: (1) a
single-vantage time series provides valid local temporal drift detection
that an implementer should absolutely rely on, and (2) multi-vantage
observation serves the distinct purpose of disambiguating observer skew
from global network state. Separating them prevents single-vantage
implementers from erroneously discounting their own telemetry.

Happy to see them hardened as two separate items in the text.

changes.author: whawk46
changes.text:
Appreciate the open release and the rigor, @stillmarcus24.

The discrimination control is the critical insight here — "a corpus that
cannot fail proves nothing" is exactly right. In adversarial and
post-settlement evaluation, negative vectors that trip an overly permissive
harness are just as load-bearing as positive ones. Having zero-dependency
reference code with explicit indeterminate/not_evaluated states gives the
working group a grounded baseline to work from.

@magentixai @TKCollective @nonlinearity This three-way consensus on claim separation is exactly where the boundary belongs.

Martin’s "Trust Lane" framing provides the clean protocol slotting, while TKCollective and nonlinearity capture the vital claim ceiling:
1. **The Payment Fingerprint** correlates that two records refer to the same authorization.
2. **The Delivery Record** binds what bytes were delivered and who signed them.
3. **The Acceptance Record** binds the counterparty’s evaluation against the terms.
